answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so voting influence depends on reachable, independently endorsed paths rather than raw identities. A dune-like sybil cluster behind a trellis of coordinated accounts, separated by a sparse external cut, has low conductance; spectral escape bounds and min-cut transitivity limit how much outside trust can enter, mathematically capping its aggregate voting weight despite any shared cipher of control.
